answer: Each agent may propose trades, but only actions backed by a scarce, nontransferable stake are counted: the protocol locks a deposit in a vault and releases it after a thread of independently verified deliveries, while slashing it for duplicate identities or failed claims. A cedar-market oracle can compare delivery records across counterparties to catch collusion. Creating sybils therefore requires funding each identity and risking real capital, not merely minting names; coordinated attackers also need enough distinct counterparties to make the records credible.
